entries.32cce6de049ecd10: Under its three-year medium-term management plan starting in fiscal 2024, the company is working to build a stable business portfolio with growth potential in order to respond proactively to changes in the business environment. The business model it aims for is a “long-term circular business that achieves sustainable growth through inter-business synergies and reinvestment centered on transportation and real estate,” and it positions the three years of the plan as a period of restart. Its priority measures are three: internal growth through improving the profitability of existing businesses (balancing the provision of social value through “mobility” with profitability, value-up investment, and inter-business collaboration); continued growth investment for sustainable growth (raising area value through real estate development, expanding real estate sales, continuing to promote overseas business, and GX investment); and strengthening the foundation for consolidated management and business promotion (human resources strategy and digital strategy). The vision word is “Creative Act. Flexibly, with creative power, toward a ‘city the world admires.’”

entries.51bbd2e0bb42297b: Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,086,179 million, up 3.0% from ¥1,054,981 million in the prior year. All businesses performed well, led by the Hotels and Resorts business. Operating revenue from external customers was ¥511,523 million for the Lifestyle Services business (¥507,604 million in the prior year), ¥223,130 million for the Transportation business (¥216,846 million), ¥212,736 million for the Real Estate business (¥204,231 million), and ¥138,789 million for the Hotels and Resorts business (¥126,298 million). In the Transportation business, Tokyu Dentetsu's passenger transport revenue was ¥152,837 million (¥150,173 million in the prior year). In the Real Estate business, sales from hotels and commercial facilities were strong and rental income rose, and there were also property sales in the asset-turnover building business.

entries.70fe91f235e9afad: This reportable segment operates department store, chain store, shopping center, credit card, cable television, advertising and video businesses. The company positions this business as contributing to raising the value of the railway lines' areas as the foundation of life in the community, and is advancing cooperation within the group to create synergies with the transportation and real estate businesses. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥511,523 million (¥507,604 million in the previous year), the largest reportable segment, accounting for just under 5 tenths of consolidated operating revenue of ¥1,086,179 million. Operating revenue including internal operating revenue between segments was ¥533,271 million (up 1.1% year on year), and the increase is attributed to Tokyu Recreation capturing a favorable movie market and to lower electricity procurement costs at Tokyu Power Supply. In the retail business, structural reform is under way, and in April 2025 the company established Tokyu Retail Management Co., Ltd., which holds 6 subsidiaries that operate the company's commercial facilities such as Tokyu Department Store and Tokyu Square. The order is by the size of operating revenue from external customers, as given in the notes to the segment information.
